About The Parameter

An AI publication that shows its sources.

The Parameter covers artificial intelligence for readers who want to understand what is happening, find tools worth testing and turn new developments into practical knowledge. We explain models, infrastructure, agents, research and regulation in plain language, and we link every significant claim to the document it came from.

Demonstration edition: the articles, bylines and dates on this site are sample material that show the editorial format. They report no real events, statistics, quotations or prices. Sources link to real, published documents.

What we cover

  • AI News: Model releases, product announcements and industry developments, read for what changed and what remains unverified.
  • Trends: Emerging AI technologies and strategic shifts, with their practical uses and current limits.
  • AI Tools: Tool and model comparisons built on criteria you can test yourself.
  • Research: What studies demonstrate, what they do not, and how safety and regulation affect real deployments.
  • Guides: Practical, repeatable workflows for using AI in research, marketing and business work.

How we work

  • We prefer primary sources: papers, filings, official data and original statements.
  • Dates are visible on every article, with updates labeled.
  • We separate what was measured from what was concluded.
  • We say plainly what remains unverified.
  • Corrections are published with the article, as described in our editorial policy.
